positiveFlows.title: THE NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION (NOAA) IS PROVIDING ONGOING FUNDING THROUGH THE NATIONAL COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM TO THE STATE OF WASHINGTON TO HELP ADMINISTER THE STATES FEDERALLY APPROVED COASTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM. THE NATIONAL COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM, UNDER THE COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT ACT, IS AN IMPORTANT VOLUNTARY FEDERAL-STATE PARTNERSHIP THAT PROTECTS, RESTORES, AND RESPONSIBLY DEVELOPS OUR NATIONS COASTAL COMMUNITIES AND RESOURCES BY BALANCING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, COASTAL USES, AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROTECTION. NOAAS INVESTMENT OF OVER $3M IS LEVERAGING OVER $2.6M IN STATE FUNDS.  THESE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT JOBS AND PROVIDE CONTINUED ASSISTANCE TO THE WASHINGTON COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM TO ADDRESS MANY IMPORTANT COASTAL ISSUES IN THE STATE INCLUDING LAND USE PLANNING, COASTAL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, SHORELINE MANAGEMENT, HABITAT PROTECTION, WETLAND MITIGATION, COASTAL HAZARDS PLANNING AND COASTAL COMMUNITY RESILIENCE. FOR EXAMPLE, ONE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON UPDATING THE RISK ASSESSMENT AND VULNERABILITY ANALYSIS SECTIONS OF THE STATE HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN, INCLUDING WORKING WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, TRIBES, STATE AGENCIES AND OTHER PARTNERS TO HELP ADVANCE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE EFFORTS AND ADDRESS EQUITY ISSUES WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF COMMUNITY RESILIENCE TO COASTAL HAZARDS AND CLIMATE CHANGE. THE FUNDING ALSO SUPPORTS ONGOING COASTAL PLANNING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL GOVERNMENTS.

WCMP PROJECT DESCRIPTION  THE NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION (NOAA) IS PROVIDING ONGOING FUNDING THROUGH THE NATIONAL COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM TO THE STATE OF WISCONSIN TO HELP ADMINISTER THE STATES FEDERALLY APPROVED COASTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM. THE NATIONAL COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM, UNDER THE COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT ACT, IS AN IMPORTANT VOLUNTARY FEDERAL-STATE PARTNERSHIP THAT PROTECTS, RESTORES, AND RESPONSIBLY DEVELOPS OUR NATIONS COASTAL COMMUNITIES AND RESOURCES BY BALANCING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, COASTAL USES, AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROTECTION. NOAAS INVESTMENT OF OVER $2.6 MILLION IS LEVERAGING OVER $2.4 MILLION IN STATE, LOCAL, AND PRIVATE FUNDS. THESE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT JOBS AND PROVIDE CONTINUED ASSISTANCE TO THE WISCONSIN COASTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM TO ADDRESS MANY IMPORTANT COASTAL ISSUES IN THE STATE, INCLUDING COASTAL HAZARDS, PUBLIC ACCESS, AND HABITAT PROTECTION AND RESTORATION. IN ADDITION, THE FUNDING SUPPORTS ONGOING COASTAL PLANNING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AND PUBLIC EDUCATION AND OUTREACH.  THE AWARD IS SUPPORTING MULTIPLE NEW INITIATIVES, SUCH AS AN EDUCATIONAL CAMPAIGN LED BY NEW WATER (GREEN BAY METROPOLITAN SEWERAGE DISTRICT) AND LOCAL PARTNERS TO RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT THE PUBLIC HEALTH RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS AND EMPOWER THE LOCAL COMMUNITIES WITH THE KNOWLEDGE AND TOOLS NEEDED TO RECOGNIZE, PREVENT, AND MITIGATE IMPACTS OF HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS.  THE AWARD IS ALSO FUNDING A NUMBER OF OTHER LOCAL PROJECTS AND INITIATIVES, INCLUDING: AN ARCHEOLOGICAL STUDY TO INVESTIGATE, MAP, AND EVALUATE FIVE SUBMERGED HISTORICAL LUMBER AND COMMERCIAL PIERS OFF THE SHORELINES IN MANITOWOC, SHEBOYGAN, AND OZAUKEE COUNTIES THE 2025-2029 UPDATE OF THE CITY OF ASHLANDS COMPREHENSIVE OUTDOOR RECREATION PLAN TO GUIDE IMPROVEMENTS FOR PARKS AND OUTDOOR RECREATION FACILITIES THE COLLECTION OF OBLIQUE PHOTOS OF WISCONSINS LAKE SUPERIOR AND LAKE MICHIGAN SHORELINES FOR THE WISCONSIN SHORELINE INVENTORY AND OBLIQUE PHOTO VIEWER ACQUISITION OF 160 ACRES IN BAYFIELD COUNTY THAT WILL PROTECT COASTAL FORESTS AND WETLANDS IN THE WHITTLESEY CREEK WATERSHED THE INSTALLATION OF AN ADA-ACCESSIBLE KAYAK LAUNCH ON THE LITTLE MANITOWOC RIVER AT LINCOLN PARK IN MANITOWOC THE DEVELOPMENT OF EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS TO TEACH THE PUBLIC ABOUT LAKE STURGEON AND PROTECTION EFFORTS FOR THEM IN THE MILWAUKEE RIVER

SPECIFICALLY, THE ILLINOIS COASTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM (CMP) WILL CREATE A NEW PROJECT MANAGER POSITION TO PROVIDE STAFF SUPPORT DIRECTLY TIED TO THIS FUNDING SOURCE. THE PROJECT MANAGER WILL COORDINATE WITH PARTNERS, DEVELOP CONTRACTING AND/OR SUBAWARD DOCUMENTS, ATTEND MEETINGS, MANAGE CONTRACTORS, ASSIST WITH INVOICING, ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING ADDITIONAL FUNDING SOURCES FOR PROJECTS, PREPARE GRANT PROPOSALS FOR CMP AND/OR PARTNERS AND PREPARE SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. THE PROJECT MANAGER WILL ALSO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT, MANAGEMENT AND PROGRESS OF PROPOSALS FOR NOAAS ANNUAL CZM BIL HABITAT RESTORATION COMPETITION. FOR PROJECTS AWARDED BIL COMPETITIVE FUNDS, THE PROJECT MANAGER WILL PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, NEPA REVIEW, ASSISTANCE WITH PRE AND POST PROJECT MONITORING, REPORTING AND TRACK FUNDS. CMP WILL SUPPORT CONCEPTUAL PLANNING AND ENGINEERING FOR A SHORELINE NATURALIZATION AND HABITAT RESTORATION PROJECT IN CHICAGO. THE PLANNING PROJECT WILL BE LED BY THE CHICAGO DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION IN PARTNERSHIP WITH GREENCORPS CHICAGO. CMPS SUPPORT WILL BRING THE PROJECT TO AT LEAST 30% ENGINEERING IN ORDER TO BE MORE SHOVEL READY FOR FUTURE FEDERAL BIL RESTORATION FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES.

DELAWARE COASTAL ZONE MANAGEMENT PROGRAM INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY-BUILDING PROJECT DESCRIPTION THE NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION (NOAA) IS PROVIDING $900,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO THE STATE OF DELAWARE THROUGH THE BIPARTISAN INFRASTRUCTURE LAW OVER THE NEXT THREE YEARS. THIS FUNDING WILL BUILD THE CAPACITY OF THE STATES FEDERALLY APPROVED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL (DNREC) TO PLAN FOR AND IMPLEMENT HABITAT RESTORATION AND CONSERVATION PROJECTS PROPOSED THROUGH FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES CONNECTED TO THE BIPARTISAN INFRASTRUCTURE LAW. SPECIFICALLY, DNREC WILL USE THESE FUNDS TO HIRE CONTRACTUAL STAFF TO IMPACT HABITAT RESTORATION AND CONSERVATION PROJECTS FOR THE ENTIRETY OF DELAWARE. DURING THE PERIOD OF THIS GRANT, FUNDS WILL SUPPORT THE CONTRACTUAL HIRE AND SUPPLIES NEEDED FOR THREE KENT CONSERVATION DISTRICT EMPLOYEES WHO WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF DELAWARE TO PREPARE FOR, APPLY FOR, MANAGE, AND MONITOR BIL FUNDED RESTORATION AND LAND CONSERVATION PROJECTS. THE THREE POSITIONS CONSIST OF A RESTORATION PROJECT COORDINATOR, RESTORATION SCIENTIST, AND A PERMITTING PLANNER. THE THREE POSITIONS WOULD BE TASKED WITH DEVELOPING PRIORITY LISTS, DEVELOPING PROPOSALS, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, CREATING MONITORING PLANS, IMPLEMENTING PLANS, ESTABLISHING BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND TRANSFERRING KNOWLEDGE, AS WELL AS ENABLING LOCAL AND REGIONAL RESTORATION PARTNERSHIPS TO NAME A FEW. DNREC FEELS VERY STRONGLY THAT COMMUNITY AND STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT IS A PRIORITY, SO THERE WILL BE JOB DUTIES ASSIGNED TO THESE POSITIONS TO ENGAGE WITH THE DELAWARE COMMUNITY TO ALLOW FOR LANDSCAPE SCALE PRIORITIZATION AND PROJECT DISCUSSIONS. THESE POSITIONS WILL HELP DNREC BUILD CAPACITY AMONG ITS NETWORKED DIVISIONS TO APPLY FOR AND ENACT FEDERALLY FUNDED HABITAT RESTORATION AND CONSERVATION PROJECTS THAT WILL IMPACT DELAWAREANS FOR GENERATIONS TO COME. ADDITIONALLY, BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND LESSONS LEARNED WILL BE DEVELOPED FROM RESTORATION PROJECTS THAT WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO OTHER LAND STEWARDS TO FURTHER THE REACH OF THESE CAPACITY FUNDS.
